reason: Console lowers every member on instances, over the instance's own counters, timers and group indentation, and the stdout, stderr, ignoreErrors, colorMode ('auto', true or false) and groupIndentation options; inspectOptions and colorMode are read the way Node's constructor reads them, so the methods that format with util.formatWithOptions (log, info, debug, warn, error, dirxml, dir, trace, assert, group and groupCollapsed) render with the instance's knobs and colors, and an invalid colorMode, a non-object inspectOptions or colorMode beside inspectOptions.colors throw Node's errors. The five output methods can also be stored as values (one bound function per instance, formatting its arguments with util.format); a table cell inspects with the table's own depth, maxArrayLength and breakLength and the instance's inspectOptions spread over them, colored per colorMode or the options' own colors, and profile, profileEnd, timeStamp and a member other than the five output methods stored off the instance have no lowering.

The heading, the util.format message, the group indentation and the shape of each frame line match Node's; the frame text is the native build's own stack, which cannot carry Node's module-loader frames, so the program compares everything but the text.
